frontend.prompt:
Make minimal UI/UX and client-side validation changes to match the new server rule (title max 80, description max 500) while preserving existing behavior for assets that already have titles >80. Implementation steps:

1) Display: continue to render title values returned by the read API unchanged (do not truncate or hide titles >80).

2) Editing form behavior:
   - Add a "touched"/"modified" flag for the title input. Consider the title field "untouched" when the form was loaded with the server value and the user has not modified it.
   - Only run/emit client-side title length validation (max 80) when the title field has been touched/modified by the user or when the user explicitly focuses and edits the title. If the title is untouched, do not block submission because its existing stored value exceeds 80.
   - For new input (when the user edits or types a title), enforce maxlength=80 on the input control and show the usual validation UX if the user attempts to enter more than 80 characters.

3) Submit payload rules:
   - Prefer sending a partial update that omits fields the user did not change. If the title was not touched, do not include the title property in the update payload.
   - If the title was touched, include the (trimmed) title value in the payload. Ensure the value sent is <=80 (client-side enforcement) and >=3 after trimming (keep existing min-length rule).

4) Error handling:
   - If the backend returns HTTP 422 for title (explicit over-limit submission), show the server validation message associated with title to the user and prevent the save.
   - If the backend returns success with an updated asset version, update UI state with the returned asset and new version.

5) Tests / acceptance checks to add in the frontend test suite:
   - Load an asset with an existing 100-character title; edit only the description and submit; expect the request to omit title and the UI to accept the save and reflect an incremented asset version from the response.
   - Attempt to edit title and submit a title >80; expect client-side blocking (if edited) or server-side 422 if client allowed it; show validation error.

Notes/constraints for implementers: Do not change trimming rules or min-length (3) behavior. If current client code cannot omit unchanged fields (e.g., always sends full resource bodies), coordinate with backend but do not assume that coordination in this task; prefer implementing omission of unchanged fields in the client where feasible.

backend.prompt:
Modify validation and update handling to roll back title maximum from 120 to 80 while preserving other existing constraints and behaviors. Implementation steps:

1) Validation rules (effective only when title is present in the incoming request):
   - Trim the incoming title using the existing trimming rule (do not change trimming behavior).
   - Enforce min length >= 3 (unchanged).
   - Enforce max length <= 80 (changed from 120 to 80) when title is explicitly provided in the request payload.

2) Update semantics (partial updates):
   - If an update request omits the title property entirely, do NOT revalidate the stored title value. Leave the stored title unchanged even if it exceeds 80 characters.
   - If the title property is present (even if equal to the stored value), validate it per step (1). If it fails max-length, return HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity with the existing validation error format and do not apply the update.

3) Read semantics:
   - Read/GET endpoints must continue to return stored titles as-is (including any titles >80). Do not modify stored values on read.

4) Versioning and persistence:
   - Continue to increment the asset version on successful updates after the rollback. A successful description-only update where title is omitted must still increment the version.
   - Ensure that rejected updates (e.g., explicit over-limit title resulting in 422) do not increment the asset version.

5) Error responses:
   - Use the existing validation error response format. For title length violations when title is present, return HTTP 422 and a validation error indicating title exceeds the 80-character maximum.

6) Tests / acceptance checks to add to backend test suite:
   - Given an asset with an existing 100-character title, issue an update that omits title and changes only description: expect success, stored title unchanged (100 chars), and asset version incremented.
   - Submit an update with title explicitly set to >80 characters: expect HTTP 422 and no version increment; validate error shape matches current validation responses.
   - Submit an update with title set to <=80 (and >=3 after trimming): expect success and a version increment.

7) Compatibility notes:
   - Do not change description max (500) nor minimum title length (3) nor trimming behavior.
   - No data migration is required: allow existing titles >80 to remain in storage.

Implementation caution: apply these rules to all update endpoints that accept modifications (PATCH, PUT or other) — for each concrete endpoint in the codebase, make sure the branch that handles updates follows the "if title omitted -> skip title validation" rule. Reuse existing validation/error formatting; do not invent a new response contract. The client will rely on HTTP 422 for explicit over-limit title submissions.
